summary:
Our project, Project Gladiators, focuses on exploring and documenting the abandoned equipment left behind by NASA missions on the Moon and Mars. These objects include scientific instruments, landers, rovers, and other mission hardware that played important roles in space exploration.

We aim to develop an educational storytelling experience that highlights the history, purpose, and significance of these discarded objects. By presenting their stories, we help people understand why this equipment was sent into space, what scientific contributions it made, and why it remains on the lunar and Martian surfaces.

This project addresses the challenge by bringing attention to forgotten equipment and preserving the legacy of space exploration through engaging and informative storytelling. It is important because these objects are not just discarded materials; they represent human curiosity, scientific achievements, technological progress, and the history of our journey beyond Earth.
details:
SPACE RELICS – An Interactive Space Museum

SPACE RELICS is an interactive educational website developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

Our project explores the historical and scientific importance of equipment left behind by NASA's lunar and Martian missions. It transforms space exploration history into an engaging digital museum where visitors can discover the stories, purposes and contributions of these objects.

The website features an interactive collection of space equipment with search and filtering options, a historical mission timeline (1966–2021), and a Planetary Atlas highlighting important mission locations. The 3D Model Bay allows users to explore an Apollo Lunar Module model interactively. The Science Wing presents information about lunar instruments, laser retroreflectors and Mars exploration equipment. An interactive quiz allows visitors to test their knowledge.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

SPACE RELICS makes space exploration history accessible to students, educators and space enthusiasts. It increases awareness of past NASA missions, encourages scientific curiosity and preserves the historical legacy of planetary exploration.

Tools and Technologies:

The website was developed using HTML for structure, CSS for styling and JavaScript for interactive functionality. It is hosted on Netlify and incorporates NASA-related educational resources and 3D models.

Creativity and Innovation:

Our project combines digital storytelling, interactive 3D visualization, historical timelines, planetary exploration maps and educational quizzes in one platform. Rather than simply listing abandoned equipment, it gives each object a story and explains its contribution to space exploration.

Factors Considered:

We considered historical accuracy, scientific relevance, accessibility, user experience and educational value. We also distinguish between equipment that is retired and equipment whose operational status is uncertain, helping visitors understand the history without making unsupported assumptions.
